title: Sovereignty Council Chief Al-Burhan Inspects Army Readiness in Blue Nile's Ed Damazin Amid RSF-SPLM-N Buildup
detail: Sudan's Sovereignty Council chairman and army chief Gen. Abdel Fattah al-Burhan visited Ed Damazin, the Blue Nile state capital, on September 3, 2026, inspecting the army's 4th Infantry Division and receiving briefings on the security and operational situation, according to an army statement. Al-Burhan stressed the need to raise preparedness, vigilance, discipline, and combat readiness, and also visited a military hospital in Damazin to check on wounded soldiers. The visit came amid escalating clashes and a reported RSF-SPLM-N buildup near the Ethiopian border, days after the RSF and allied SPLM-N (al-Hilu) fighters claimed to have seized the army's Bakori and Sirkam bases southeast of the city and thousands of civilians fled toward Damazin from southern and western Blue Nile.

title: UN Fact-Finding Mission: Transnational Networks Spanning UAE, Colombia, Chad, Libya and Somalia Fuel RSF War Effort
detail: The UN Human Rights Council-mandated Fact-Finding Mission for Sudan reported on September 3, 2026 that it found reasonable grounds to believe a transnational network of companies and individuals based in the UAE, Colombia, Chad, Libya, and Somalia supplied the RSF with weapons, logistics, training, and foreign personnel — including roughly 2,000 Colombian contractors operating combat drones and advanced weapons systems across Darfur and Kordofan. Mission chair Mohamad Chande Othman said 'this external support has not brought greater protection for civilians. Instead, civilians are paying the price through attacks on homes, hospitals, schools, markets and places of refuge,' and investigators linked foreign-trained fighters to the 2025 Zamzam camp and El Fasher massacres. Both the SAF and RSF have received enhanced drone capabilities from foreign backers, the report found, documenting drone attacks on civilian infrastructure by both sides that may amount to war crimes, and it urged the Security Council to expand the arms embargo Sudan-wide with stronger enforcement.

title: Kurmuk Commissioner Accuses Ethiopia of Hosting Four UAE-Backed RSF Training Camps Near Blue Nile Border
detail: Abdelati Mohamed El Faki, the Sudanese-government-aligned commissioner of Kurmuk in southeastern Blue Nile state, said on September 3, 2026 that the RSF was running four camps inside Ethiopia — Fano (roughly 40km from Kurmuk), Dabbous and Abramo (southwest of Asosa), and Jabal al-Dush, which he said hosts drone launch facilities roughly 30km from Kurmuk — to train RSF fighters and foreign mercenaries and stage drone operations, allegedly under Ethiopian intelligence supervision and with Emirati financing. Sudan Tribune said it could not independently verify the claim; Ethiopia has previously denied Sudanese government accusations that it facilitates arms transfers or training for the RSF, and the UAE has repeatedly rejected allegations that it backs the paramilitary group militarily.
